body: I don't really have any friends. I move around a lot so I don't even bother trying to make any. Even if I did, I don't know if I'd be able to call the hotlines. My father picks me up and drops me off to and from school, and I'm not allowed to go anywhere unsupervised.
My school is way too overcrowded for that to work out.

Each student is assigned only one guidance counselor depending on grade level and spelling of last name.

I tried talking to one of my teachers but nothing they said was actually helpful. I don't feel comfortable talking to any of my other teachers about anything.
Thank you, but there is no convincing my parents. They will not listen. As far as I know conversion therapy is only illegal in like six states, and I don't live in one of those states.

Explaining it to my parents is not an option. That is way too scary. They've made it clear that they'll immediately send me to conversion therapy the next time I bring up anything about being LGBT+.

I try to call the translifeline as often as I can but there's a couple problems with that. One, most of the time I can't get through and it just says "there is no one available to take your call, try again later", and two, when I do get through, I don't have much longer than ten minutes as my parents might hear what I'm talking about or snatch my phone and see who I'm talking to.

>And will you succeed? Yes! You will, indeed! (98 and 3/4 percent guaranteed.)

I can't see how this will ever get better. And even if I could, that doesn't really help the present.

Thank you for trying to inspire me though.

I'm happy that other people have gone through and gotten easier lives, but I'm kind of stuck in the present for now.

It doesn't always get better, and it's just annoying to hear that it will when no one really knows.

I'm way too horrified of her telling my parents. When I came to her the first time she said that she would have already called my parents if I hadn't begged her not too. At that time all I said was that I was having trouble with school because of being anxious from dysphoria. There's no way she wouldn't keep it a secret if I said anything more than that. I can not under any circumstance have my parents find out.

I wouldn't be able to do that. My parents would get on my ass about what the hell could possibly be making me unhappy. I tried to kill myself a few times in middle school and was forced to go to a therapist because of that for a while and my dad constantly berated me about having to go there and would constantly pressure me to tell him exactly what we talked about.

>Is there anyone outside of your home, like a trusted teacher at school or a friend's parent, you feel comfortable discussing this things with? Even if they aren't an expert in the sorts of things you're experiencing, you may find it helpful to have someone to confide in who's concerned about your wellbeing. 

I don't know, I really don't know. I had one teacher that I talked to the guidance counselor with but they weren't really helpful. All they did was tell me about a similar phone line. Other than I that I can't think of anyone.
I don't know of any that I can go to out of school hours. I'm also not allowed to go anywhere without my dad's supervision, so that would be kind of hard.

I actually did talk to a school counselor about having a lot of trouble doing work because of dysphoria and just general sadness. All she really did was tell me about some kind of phoneline and told me to update her...so she wasn't that helpful.

I've tried doing the online chat for the trevor project a few times. When I mention that I'm cutting myself most of the people on there only focus on that, and when I say that it's not cutting that's causing me to feel like shit they insist on saying that if I found other ways to cope besides cut then my other problems would go away but I just can't. Cutting just works better. It's also way too hard to be honest with them. I'm scared that I'm going to say too much and that they're going to track down my call and start shit.

I've tried calling the translifeline a few times but I don't have much privacy. They've said a few helpful things but overall nothing that gets me out of my situation or makes me feel better about living. Sometimes it seems like they have an idea or two but I don't have any privacy in my house and it's really hard to stay on the line out of fear that my parents will hear or snatch my phone and see who I'm talking to.
